_about: What the port's lighting reads that no level file carries. Levels carry their own ambient,
emissive and lightmaps as metadata/eth_* keys (sim/Lighting.hpp); this is what the ORIGINAL'S
SCRIPT sets over them. Enhanced's out/parity/specs/lighting/design_port.md, section 5.9, and
Only what a built step reads is here: the two ambient lights the script sets (G3, step 45), and
the normal maps' green and the halo scale (G5, step 49), the 16-bit framebuffer (G6, step 55), and
the script's emissive overrides on the levels that set ignore_emissive (CMP-1, planning step 166), and
how a static lit sprite's lightmap is baked at level load (CMP-14, planning step 196).

_source: Moved from art.json's darkest block. Game's level-properties reader does
CheckCustomData('darkest') and, when it is set, SetAmbientLight(DARKEST_AMBIENT_LIGHT); that
one call is the whole of what the flag does there. DARKEST_AMBIENT_LIGHT is built at
Game.angelscript bytes 306783..306841 as vector3(0.01, 0.01, 0.01): very nearly black, not
black. It REPLACES the level file's own <Ambient> - level21c (4-22) says 0.5 and draws at
0.01 - and ETHCallback_fire_signal sets it again when a torch is put back out
(torch.json, signal).
Moved from torch.json's ambient.lit. ETHCallback_light_off's `delete` branch, run on the
frame after the torch is shot, calls SetAmbientLight(0.1, 0.1, 0.25) - lighter than
darkest's 0.01, and blue, but not lit - then lightenAllBackgroundEntitities and
GenerateLightmaps (bytes 467198..473086). Those two are the design's step G6, not this.
Decoded, not tested for. The original's light shader, hPixelLightDiff.ps (shaders.h:1261-1304 in
the shipped library; Enhanced's engine_math.md 4.5), decodes a normal-map texel c as
-(2 (c - 0.5)) and dots it with (P - L) in Ethanon's world, whose y points DOWN the screen. So a
green above one half faces down the image, where the port's world is y-up: the engine flips it
(MaterialComponent::Sprite2DLight::normalYDown). The port's torch pass on the player (step 49)
is the measurement that would show the other sense.
What every <Light><HaloBitmap> halo's formula colour, <Color> x haloBrightness x the owner's live
particle ratio (ETHRenderEntity.cpp:354-388), is multiplied by. Ethanon has no such factor: 1 is
its formula. The design leaves the number to the halo gate (design_port.md 5.5 and 8), and the
gate says one is needed: at 1 the port reads 8.94 of 255 on 1-01's LM_E<1_halo blocks against
the original (asked 6.0), and Enhanced's fit, drawn with 1x art at the brightness the port drew
(its torch's flame 10 of 12 live at frame 420), reads 8.88 there, so it is the brightness and
not the art. The fit finds x0.5 of the formula's maximum on the arch with the strongest halo
signal in both 1-01 and 1-09 (fit.md 6).
_measured: Step 49, frame 420, the port against the original, LM_E<1_halo on 1-01 / on 1-09 / noLM_E=1_halo
both LM_E<1_halo rows: drawn with 1x art the fit's own model reads at least 5.84 on 1-09 at any
brightness (2.97 with the original's hd art), and above 6 on 1-01 past an effective 0.55.
_note: 0.6 is the value those rows favour: 1-01 passes and 1-09 misses by 0.17, inside the 1x floor. It
is tuned to one frame's flame. Over 20 s the torch's flame is 0.7265 live (test_mp_layer), so
0.6 draws the halo at 0.44 of the formula on average, where 0.69 would match the fit's 0.5 on
average and 1 would be Ethanon's own arithmetic. For the owner, and for plan_port System 6.
System 6 landed in step 66 (the level's hd and fullhd art). At frame 420 and 0.6 the halo rows
then read 1-01 LM_E<1_halo 3.28, LM_E=1_halo 1.16; 1-09 LM_E<1_halo 2.95, noLM_E=1_halo 3.50
(asked 6.0 each; 5.59, 20.72, 5.99 and 3.80 with 1x art), so the value was not reopened.

_source: The original asks Android for a 5/6/5 surface and draws into it without dithering: GL2JNIView.java:94
and ConfigChooser.java:48-67 in the shipped APK (Enhanced's engine_math.md 0.2). Enhanced's fit
of its pixels scores 0.28 of 255 on dark sprites with the 5/6/5 step and 0.62 without (fit.md 9).
The engine quantises the composite (RenderSettings::OutputQuantize::Rgb565); the screen overlay
drawn after it - the HUD, the pause, the menus - is not quantised.
THE SCRIPT'S EMISSIVE OVERRIDES (CMP-1, planning step 166; the design's section 5.8). From Enhanced's
out/parity/asbc/all_functions.txt, md5 48fe65ce8baea16b94ed84d8d7be84b0:
Game::readProperties (Game.angelscript bytes 116676..118260), called by Game::preLoop #33 before
anything is scaled: #53 emissiveValue = 0; #55-66 CheckCustomData('ignore_emissive') == 3 (the
uint datum type, ETHCustomDataManager.h:34-42: DT_UINT = 3), and only then #68-70
Game.ignoreEmissive = true and #72-82 emissiveValue = GetFloat('door_emissive') - the jump at #66
skips #72-82 too, so a level that carries door_emissive WITHOUT ignore_emissive (4-02 to 4-19, all
at 0) never has it read; #223-237 Game.door = SeekEntity('door.ent'), #268-283 SeekEntity('door')
when that is null; #285-300, when Game.ignoreEmissive is set, door.SetEmissiveColor(vector3(
emissiveValue, emissiveValue, emissiveValue)). The datum's VALUE is never read, only its type, so
the port's test is the key's presence on the first `properties` node, which is the same test on
every shipped level: the original's .esc files carry it as <Type>uint</Type><Value>1</Value> on
exactly 78 levels (2-01 to 2-32, 3-01 to 3-32, 4-01 and 4-20 to 4-32), door_emissive as float 0.1
on the 46 of those in chapters 3 and 4 and not at all on chapter 2's 32 (read as 0, #72-82's
GetFloat of an absent datum and emissiveValue's own #53 start).
Game::preLoop (bytes 112536..114414) #355-393, after the character is built (#75) and the layers
are added: when Game.ignoreEmissive is set, #360-364 emissiveValue = vector3(0, 0, 0), #366-381
vector3(0.2, 0.2, 0.2) when g_currentWorld == 2 (#367 CMPIi 2, #368 JP past it, #370 JZ into it),
#384-392 character.getEntity().SetEmissiveColor(emissiveValue). g_currentWorld is the 0-based
world openLevel passes (main.angelscript bytes 312129..312230, openWorld 312230..312318, and its
own start at 0, bytes 296495..296532), so 2 is chapter 3.
Game::Game (bytes 110437..111736) #304-305 starts Game.ignoreEmissive false.
Nothing else of the listing writes the character's emissive (the only SetEmissiveColor call sites are
blinkEmissive, ETHCallback_dark_dragon, ETHCallback_minion, setBackgroundTilesEmissiveColor, which
paints pilar.ent alone, and these two), and the door's only here. It replaces the .ent's own values,
which stay what art.json and the level's node say on every other level: dark_mage.ent's (1, 1, 1)
and door.ent's 0.7. door_bg.ent (black.bmp and the red flame, emissive 1) is left alone by the script.
Fits (Enhanced's out/parity/program/R4b/CMP, the comparison of step 165): 4-01's player reads
HOW A STATIC LIT SPRITE'S LIGHTMAP IS MADE (CMP-14, planning step 196; sim/LightmapBake.hpp). At a screen of
480 px or more the original does NOT read the add<id>.png files it ships: Game's shouldUsePrerenderedLights is
GetScreenSize().y < 480 (Enhanced's out/parity/asbc/all_functions.txt:61740-61750, bytes 313283..313382, md5
48fe65ce8baea16b94ed84d8d7be84b0: CMPIf 480f; TS), preLoop calls EnablePreLoadedLightmapsFromFile(true) only then
(listing :61783-61788), the flag defaults to false (ETHScriptWrapper.cpp:39), so LoadLightmaps() at the end of
LoadScene runs GenerateLightmaps() (ETHScriptWrapper.Scene.cpp:198-204, :607-609), which bakes every static
applyLight sprite into a render target of its BITMAP SIZE IN UNITS, one texel per unit (ETHLightmapGen.cpp:57-58,
ETHScene.cpp:336-427): 2.8125 px a texel on the 1280x720 rig. The shipped files are half the sprite per axis (730 of
730), so the port drew a lightmap twice as coarse as the original's (Enhanced's out/parity/program/MEAS/CMP-14/
result.txt, 3A-3E: the lattice test, the dose-response, the offline model). The arithmetic of the bake is the
calibration judge's resolved choices R1-R20 (out/parity/program/CMP14/pre/calibration.md).
The OUTPUT pitch, in units per texel; the light is always evaluated at the unit lattice. 1 is the original at a
screen of 480 px or more (ETHLightmapGen.cpp:57-58). 2 is the pitch of the shipped files and is the G0 self-check
of planning step 196 (with the target at 8 bits a channel, below): the unit bake reduced 2:1 by `reduction`
reproduces the shipped add<id>.png to the tolerance of calibration.md section 4.3. Only 1 and the reduction's
factor are accepted.
The target the bake draws into: GL_RGB / GL_UNSIGNED_SHORT_5_6_5, one store per light into a black temporary
target and an add of the temporaries (GLES2Texture.cpp:150-170; gs2d/src/Video.h:139; ETHLightmapGen.cpp:86-168),
so a channel holds 31, 63 and 31 levels and the lightmap is the SATURATING INTEGER SUM of the per-light levels
(calibration R8). 8, 8, 8 is for the G0 self-check only: the shipped files are 8-bit data (calibration R11).
_note: Nothing in the source says how the float-to-fixed store rounds, and the shipped files are 8-bit smooth data that
cannot rank the rules (calibration R9, spec U1). Nearest is the engine's own Rgb565 rule, fitted to the original's
5/6/5 FRAMEBUFFER (fit.md 9: 0.28 of 255 with the step against 0.62 without), and is what a GL float-to-fixed gives.
The other word the reader accepts is truncate.

_source: Consulted only when units_per_texel is 2 (the G0 self-check). The shipped add<id>.png files are NOT a render at
2 units a texel: they are the unit bake reduced 2:1 by a Catmull-Rom filter (Keys a = -0.5, support scaled by 2,
Pillow's BICUBIC) and stored as 8-bit RGB (calibration.md section 0 and R10; calibA s11/s20, judge j08). Separable,
output texel k centred at unit 2k + 1, taps over source texels 2k - 3 .. 2k + 4, MIRROR edge (index -1 reads 0, n
reads n - 1), computed in double and rounded to the nearest 8-bit value, clamped to [0, 255]. The taps sum to the
denominator, so a constant stays constant.
